key_insight: A single-stage Huffman encoder replaces the traditional three-stage pipeline (frequency analysis, codebook generation, codebook transmission) so lossless compression can be done on-the-fly with negligible extra latency and no per-message codebook overhead.
problem_solved: Eliminates the compute, latency and data overheads of on-the-fly frequency analysis and codebook exchange that make Huffman compression impractical for low-latency distributed training and serving of LLMs.
method: Design a single-pass encoder that deterministically maps symbols to Huffman codewords without a separate frequency-analysis stage.
Use a compact, canonical/static codebook or a derivable, synchronized codebook across accelerators to avoid per-transfer codebook transmission.
Integrate streaming-friendly, low-overhead encoding into the communication path so compression adds minimal CPU and latency cost.
impact: Makes lossless Huffman compression practical for bandwidth-constrained distributed ML workloads, reducing network traffic and communication bottlenecks during LLM training and inference while preserving zero-loss accuracy.

paper_title: Single-Stage Huffman Encoder for ML Compression
